nama_domain: Youth Unemployment & Anti-Hustle Culture (the involution -> lying-flat -> let-it-rot -> rat-people continuum: mass graduate under-employment producing a self-organised culture of withdrawal, anti-productivity and nocturnal social retreat)
kategori: Ketenagakerjaan (Labour & Employment) — with heavy spillover into Pendidikan (Higher Education), Kesehatan Mental (Public Mental Health), Ekonomi Konsumsi (Consumption/Demand) and Stabilitas Sosial-Politik
tahun_mulai_china: 2020-2021 for the mainstream break, with a clear five-stage genealogy: (1) 内卷 'involution' entered mass vocabulary in 2020 (the viral Tsinghua 'involuted king' cycling-while-coding photo, Sep 2020); (2) 躺平 'tang ping / lying flat' became the defining term in April-May 2021 (Luo Huazhong's Baidu Tieba post 'Lying Flat Is Justice', ~April 2021, viral May 2021, named a buzzword of the year 2021); (3) 摆烂 'bai lan / let it rot' in 2022 (active abandonment rather than passive rest); (4) 鼠鼠文学 'rat literature' and 孔乙己文学 'Kong Yiji literature' in early 2023 (self-deprecating 'I am but a rat' register; the degree as a scholar's gown you cannot take off); (5) 老鼠人 / 低能量老鼠人 'rat people / low-energy rat people' which exploded in March-April 2025. The economic trigger sequence: 2020-2022 COVID + platform/tutoring/property crackdowns, record graduate cohorts from 2021, and the collapse of the property-wealth channel from 2021-2022.
pemain_kunci_china: This is a bottom-up cultural trend, so the 'key players' are platforms, symbolic originators, and the institutions reacting to it. Platforms/amplifiers: Douyin (抖音) — the single largest carrier of 老鼠人 vlogs; Xiaohongshu (RED/小红书) — where '低能量' topped the trending list; Bilibili (B站) — home of 鼠鼠文学 and 摆烂 video culture; Baidu Tieba (百度贴吧) — birthplace of both 躺平 (Luo Huazhong, 2021) and much rat-literature; Weibo (微博) — mainstreaming and state-media pushback; Zhihu (知乎) — the long-form debate layer; Kuaishou (快手) — small-town/rural variant. Symbolic originators: Luo Huazhong (骆华忠, the original 'lying-flat master'); anonymous Chinese overseas students in the UK who coined the 'rat person' day-in-the-life vlog format. Commercial actors that monetised the meme (March-April 2025): Meituan (美团), Tmall (天猫), Alibaba 1688, Midea (美的), Guoquan Shihui (锅圈食汇), snack and tissue brands, plus the sleep-economy/宅经济 cluster (short-lease studio rentals, cheap meal boxes, sleep aids, mobile/idle games). Institutional actors: National Bureau of Statistics (NBS), Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security (MOHRSS), Ministry of Education (MOE), Xinhua/People's Daily/Guangming Daily (the discourse-management arm), the Communist Youth League, and from July 2025 the Central Financial and Economic Affairs Commission which turned '反内卷' (anti-involution) into official macro policy.
apa_yang_terjadi_di_china: China has produced, in roughly five years, the world's most articulated youth counter-culture of refusal — and the underlying driver is a labour-market arithmetic failure, not laziness. Mechanism: (a) Higher-education expansion outran the creation of graduate-grade jobs. Annual college graduates rose from ~8.7 million (2019) to 11.79 million (2024), 12.22 million (2025) and a record 12.7 million (2026), while the sectors that historically absorbed them — internet platforms, private tutoring, real estate, finance — were simultaneously hit by regulatory crackdowns (2021), a property bust (2021-) and cost-cutting. (b) The result is 'involution' (内卷): more credentials, more hours, more test-taking for the same or shrinking prize. Master's degrees and civil-service exams become defensive purchases rather than upgrades. (c) When effort stops paying, the rational individual response is to reduce effort and consumption to the point where the system cannot extract more — 躺平 (lie flat): minimal work, minimal spending, no marriage, no mortgage, no children. (d) 摆烂 (let it rot, 2022) radicalised this from strategic rest to demonstrative self-abandonment. (e) 鼠鼠文学 (2023) supplied the emotional grammar — speaking of oneself in the third person as a sewer rat, a creature with no claim on dignity — which pairs with 孔乙己文学 (March 2023), where a degree becomes a gown you cannot remove to take a manual job. (f) 老鼠人 (2025) is the behavioural end-state: a nocturnal, low-stimulus, low-desire, delivery-fed existence in a rented room — wake around 11:00, scroll in bed, first meal around 15:00, no daylight, no social contact, sleep after midnight, repeat. It is not primarily protest and it is not clinical hikikomori; it is a self-mocking identity (自黑) that converts economic humiliation into shareable comedy. Scale of the phenomenon is genuinely mass: Douyin generated more than a dozen related hashtags in 2025, with a single topic passing 1.47 billion views and cross-platform totals reported in the multi-billions. Critically, the state's response evolved from moral condemnation (Xinhua calling lying flat 'shameful' in 2021, censorship of tang-ping forums) to partial adoption of the youth diagnosis: by July 2025 Xi Jinping's own agenda item was '反内卷' — rectifying 'involutionary competition' — applied to firms and local governments rather than to individuals. In other words, the state accepted the word the youth invented, then redirected it at industrial price wars. Meanwhile the material adaptations institutionalised: 全职儿女 ('full-time children' paid an allowance by parents for domestic labour and companionship), 慢就业 ('slow employment' — deliberately delaying entry), mass exam-taking (3.718 million applicants cleared screening for the 2026 civil-service exam, ~2.9x the 2019 level, against ~38,100 posts), and a shift of graduates into delivery, livestream and other flexible work inside a ~200-million-strong flexible-employment pool.
data_skala_china: LABOUR MARKET: Urban surveyed unemployment, ages 16-24 excluding students — record 21.3% (June 2023, old methodology, after which publication was suspended for six months); series resumed Dec 2023 on a new student-excluding methodology; 18.9% in August 2025 (record under the new series); 17.8% July 2025; 16.9% Nov 2025; 16.5% Dec 2025; ~15.8% average for 2025; 16.3% Jan 2026; 16.1% Feb 2026; 15.6% May 2026; 14.9% June 2026 (lowest in a year). Estimates of roughly 20 million jobless urban Gen Z circulate in the international press [uncertain — derived, not an NBS series]. GRADUATE SUPPLY: 11.79m (2024) -> 12.22m (2025) -> 12.7m (2026, +480,000 y/y), a record every year. EXAM DEFENSIVENESS: 2026 national civil-service exam (国考) — 3.718 million applicants passed qualification review, an all-time high and ~2.9x the 2019 figure, for ~38,100 posts (the first year the post count was cut, by ~1,600); hottest single post attracted over 7,000 applicants (reported ratios above 7,222:1); postgraduate entrance exam (考研) fell for a third consecutive year to 3.43 million in 2026, and for the first time civil-service applicants exceeded graduate-school applicants. MEME SCALE: #老鼠人 — a single Douyin topic exceeded 1.47 billion views in 2025; aggregated cross-platform view counts reported at close to 20 billion, of which Douyin alone accounts for roughly 10 billion [uncertain — Chinese marketing-industry estimates, not audited platform data; the widely-cited conservative figure is 'over 2 billion views']; #低能量 topics passed 100 million views and topped Xiaohongshu's hot list; brand pile-on within weeks (Meituan, Tmall, 1688, Midea, Guoquan and others posting self-deprecating 'we are rat people too' creative in March-April 2025). ADJACENT DEMOGRAPHICS: marriage registrations have fallen for a decade and are roughly half their 2013-2014 peak; births fell to ~7.92 million in 2025 from 9.54 million in the 2024 dragon-year rebound [uncertain — the 2025 figure and the size of the drop vary across reports]; flexible/gig employment around 200 million people. POLICY: 17 inter-ministerial measures (April 2025) with one-off hiring subsidies, social-insurance subsidies extended for SOE graduate hiring to 31 Dec 2026, and a target of training 1 million graduates and youths in 2025.
fase_tren_di_china: Mature and institutionalised, moving into a managed/co-opted phase rather than declining. Evidence for 'mature': the vocabulary has completed a full generational cycle (involution -> lie flat -> let it rot -> rat literature -> rat people) with each stage more behavioural and less rhetorical than the last; the 2025 rat-people wave was commercialised by mainstream brands within roughly a month of going viral, which is the classic signature of a subculture crossing into mass culture. Evidence for 'managed/co-opted': the state stopped fighting the diagnosis and adopted the word — '反内卷' became formal economic policy from July 2025 (Central Financial and Economic Affairs Commission, 1 July 2025) and was written into the Fourth Plenum decision of October 2025 — while public-opinion units (e.g. provincial 舆情 monitoring reports in mid-2025) now analyse 老鼠人 as a sentiment indicator rather than as deviance to be censored. Evidence against 'declining': youth unemployment set a new record under the current methodology in August 2025, i.e. after the meme peaked, and although the rate fell through the first half of 2026 (14.9% in June 2026), the graduate cohort keeps hitting records. The cultural form will keep mutating (a successor label after 老鼠人 should be expected roughly every 12-24 months); the underlying condition is structural and will outlast any one label.
puncak_tren_china: Two distinct peaks must be separated. (1) STRUCTURAL PEAK of the underlying labour distress: mid-2023 on the old measurement (21.3%, June 2023, nationwide but concentrated in first- and second-tier cities and in the post-crackdown internet/tutoring/property corridors of Beijing, Shanghai, Shenzhen, Hangzhou); a second, methodologically different peak in August 2025 (18.9%). (2) CULTURAL/ATTENTION PEAK of each label: 躺平 peaked in mid-to-late 2021; 摆烂 in 2022; 鼠鼠/孔乙己文学 in the first half of 2023; 老鼠人 peaked sharply in March-April 2025 (media crossover in March, brand-marketing saturation in April) with a long tail through late 2025 when international media picked it up. Geographically the rat-people wave is a big-city rental-room phenomenon (Beijing, Shanghai, Guangzhou, Shenzhen, Hangzhou, Chengdu, Wuhan) plus a distinctive overseas-student origin node (Chinese students in the UK), and it overlaps with the returnee and post-layoff cohorts in tech and education services.
status_di_indonesia: Split status. The AESTHETIC/DISCURSIVE layer has already arrived (masif, effectively simultaneous): Indonesian media, TikTok and campus discourse covered 'manusia tikus' during 2025, and the domestic vocabulary of refusal — mager, rebahan, healing, self-reward, nolep, quiet quitting, #KaburAjaDulu — is already mainstream. The STRUCTURAL condition (record youth unemployment, graduate under-employment, credential devaluation) is also already present and worsening. What has NOT arrived at scale is the specific Chinese end-state — full economic withdrawal financed by family wealth, sustained nocturnal isolation as a mass lifestyle, and voluntary exit from the labour force by educated urban youth. Indonesian youth today mostly cannot afford to withdraw: they convert the same despair into gig work (ojol, freelancing), migration ambitions, informal hustling, or street politics. So: 'baru mulai' on the behavioural layer, 'sudah masuk masif' on the meme layer, 'sudah masiv' on the underlying labour-market condition.
contoh_konkret_indonesia: (a) #KaburAjaDulu — emerged December 2024, went viral on X and TikTok in February 2025; began as an emigration-tips channel and became a general vote of no-confidence in Indonesian wages, prices, taxes and bureaucracy; commented on by UGM, SBM ITB and covered by CNN Indonesia, CNBC Indonesia and foreign media. This is Indonesia's functional equivalent of tang ping, but its vector is EXIT (abroad) rather than STASIS (bed). (b) 'Indonesia Gelap' protests (February 2025) and the far larger August 2025 wave (25-31 August 2025; ~3,195 people detained nationwide; spread to 30+ provinces; catalysed by DPR allowances and then by the death of 21-year-old ojol driver Affan Kurniawan under a police vehicle on 28 August; One Piece Jolly Roger as the protest emblem) — the VOICE channel for the same generational grievance. (c) Quiet quitting and anti-hustle discourse: Populix (2024) reported that over 63% of Indonesian workers under 30 had deliberately disengaged at work [uncertain]; a Jakpat survey (February 2026) reported 41% of Indonesian Gen Z actively refuse work outside contracted hours [uncertain]; 'kerja ya kerja, tapi secukupnya' has become a recognisable norm. (d) The rebahan/mager/nolep vocabulary, 'healing' culture, doom-scrolling and doom-spending, plus a large nocturnal mobile-gaming population — the raw behavioural substrate the Chinese meme would map onto. (e) Frugal living as mass practice: 'makan tabungan' (dipping into savings) with 76.3% of surveyed households drawing down savings when expenses exceed income, and a middle class that shrank to ~46.7 million in 2025 (-1.1 million y/y). (f) Institutional recognition: growing national commentary on 'sarjana menganggur' (unemployed graduates), including from senior figures, and Kemendiktisaintek's 2026 programme rationalisation (122 study programmes closed).
data_skala_indonesia: YOUTH LABOUR: Open unemployment rate for ages 15-24 was 16.26% (November 2025) and 16.36% (February 2026) — the highest of any age cohort, and rising year-on-year while the 25-59 cohort improved by 0.11pp; the national TPT was 4.68-4.74% over the same period with 7.24 million unemployed (Feb 2026) and 7.35 million (Nov 2025). In August 2024 there were ~3.93 million unemployed aged 15-24, of whom ~2.81 million had never worked at all — i.e. roughly half of all Indonesian unemployment is young, and most young unemployment is first-job failure, not job loss. GRADUATES: unemployed holders of D4/S1/S2/S3 rose from 1,010,652 (Feb 2025) to 1,033,737 (Feb 2026); TPT for tertiary graduates 6.13% and for SMK 7.74% — both above the national average, the textbook signature of credential devaluation. NEET: close to 10 million Gen Z (ages 15-24) classified NEET as of 2023 (~9.9 million), disproportionately women. DEMOGRAPHY: Gen Z is ~74.93 million people, 27.94% of the population (2025). MIDDLE CLASS: 46.7 million in 2025 (down 1.1 million, a steeper fall than 2024's -400,000), with an 'aspiring middle class' of ~142 million sitting one shock away from poverty. DIGITAL SUBSTRATE (the transmission medium): 230 million internet users (80.5% of population, +8.7%), 180 million social-media identities (62.9%), TikTok advertising reach ~180 million, ~21 hours 50 minutes per week on social media and online video (Digital 2026 / DataReportal). MENTAL HEALTH BASELINE: I-NAMHS 2022 — 34.9% of adolescents (≈15.5 million) reported a mental-health problem in the past 12 months and 1 in 20 (≈2.45 million) met criteria for a disorder, anxiety most common; roughly one third of Indonesian Gen Z are reported to experience burnout before age 25 [uncertain]. EDUCATION SUPPLY: tertiary gross enrolment ~45% (2023) versus China's 60.8% (2024); 122 study programmes closed in 2026 while 1,200+ new programmes opened, mostly vocational/applied.
estimasi_lag_tahun: Dimension-specific, and deliberately not a single number. (a) MEME/AESTHETIC LAYER: 0-1 year — effectively simultaneous. 老鼠人 broke in China in March 2025 and was being explained to Indonesian audiences in Indonesian-language media within the same year; algorithmic content diffusion has collapsed this lag to near zero. (b) DISCOURSE OF REFUSAL AS A NAMED MOVEMENT: ~3-4 years. China's tang ping moment was 2021; Indonesia's functional equivalent (#KaburAjaDulu plus mainstream quiet-quitting discourse) arrived December 2024-2025. (c) STRUCTURAL CONDITION (record youth unemployment + graduate oversupply): ~2-3 years, and closing fast — China's record was 2023, Indonesia's youth series hit its recent high in 2025-2026. (d) BEHAVIOURAL END-STATE (mass voluntary withdrawal, nocturnal low-desire living financed by family): 8-12 years, and possibly never in the same form — this requires household wealth Indonesian families do not have (see faktor_pembatal_transfer). (e) POLICY RECOGNITION AND INSTRUMENTS (hiring subsidies targeted at youth, a national anti-involution frame, mass retraining of graduates): ~4-6 years behind; China ran 17 coordinated inter-ministerial measures in 2025, Indonesia has no equivalent youth-specific employment package of comparable scale. HEADLINE: treat the cultural lag as 0-2 years, the structural-labour lag as 2-3 years, the withdrawal-behaviour lag as 8-12 years (partially cancelled), and the policy lag as 4-6 years and widening.
bukti_historical_lag: (1) Meme diffusion is already near-zero-lag: the Labubu/Pop Mart wave reached Indonesia in 2025 against a Chinese scale-up of 2019-2020 for the product, but the CONTENT wave moved within months; likewise 'brain rot', 'quiet quitting' and 'doom spending' entered Indonesian usage within one year of their Anglophone/Chinese peaks. Cultural lag has compressed from years to months since TikTok/Reels reached ~180 million Indonesian reach. (2) Labour-market consequence lag runs 3-5 years, consistent with the sibling analysis in this research set: China's algorithmic-exploitation reckoning peaked September 2020 and produced binding guidance by July 2021, while Indonesia's equivalent reached presidential level only in 2025-2026; China's youth-unemployment record was mid-2023, Indonesia's graduate-unemployment issue became a headline political fight in 2025. (3) Credential devaluation followed the same path with a lag: China's 孔乙己文学 (the useless-degree lament) went viral in March 2023; Indonesia's mass 'sarjana menganggur' discourse and the data showing tertiary TPT (6.13%) above the national average (4.68%) became a standing national argument in 2025-2026 — a 2-3 year gap. (4) Education-system response lag is wider: China's Ministry of Education ordered ~20% of programmes optimised in March 2023 and cut 12,200 undergraduate programmes over 2021-2025; Indonesia closed 122 programmes in 2026 — the same policy instinct, roughly three years later and two orders of magnitude smaller. (5) Counter-evidence for a REVERSE element: Indonesia's youth political explosion (August 2025, 30+ provinces, ~3,195 detained) has no Chinese analogue at all; on the 'voice' dimension Indonesia is ahead, not behind.
tipe_lag: HYBRID, and the mix is the whole story: LEAPFROG/SIMULTANEOUS on the symbolic layer (memes of refusal arrive within months via algorithmic diffusion), LAGGARD by 2-3 years on the labour-market structure and by 4-6 years on policy machinery, PARTIALLY CANCELLED on the specific behavioural end-state (mass withdrawal requires family wealth Indonesia lacks), and REVERSE on the expression channel (Indonesian youth externalise the same grievance into street protest and emigration years before Chinese youth internalised theirs into withdrawal — Hirschman's EXIT and VOICE where China got LOYALTY-as-passivity). The most consequential asymmetry is not timing but income: Indonesia is reaching Chinese-level youth unemployment at roughly USD 5,000 GDP per capita, whereas China hit its record at roughly USD 12,600-13,000 — a 'worse-outcome laggard' pattern, i.e. the same distress with a much thinner cushion.
probabilitas_transfer: Tinggi (High) for the cultural/discursive form and for anti-hustle norms in the workplace; Sedang (Medium) for a genuinely mass, sustained withdrawal behaviour among urban educated youth; Rendah-Sedang (Low-Medium) for the full Chinese end-state of long-run family-financed non-participation ('full-time children' as a recognised social role).
alasan_probabilitas: High for the cultural layer because every precondition is already satisfied: 230 million internet users, 180 million TikTok-reachable people, ~22 hours a week of social video, a youth unemployment rate (16.36%, Feb 2026) statistically comparable to China's, tertiary graduates whose unemployment rate (6.13%) exceeds the national average, ~9.9 million NEET Gen Z, a shrinking middle class, and an existing native vocabulary (mager, rebahan, nolep, healing, quiet quitting) that the Chinese frame slots into without translation friction. Memes of refusal are cheap to adopt and socially rewarding — they convert private failure into shared comedy. Medium for the behavioural layer because Indonesia lacks the two enabling conditions that made Chinese lying-flat survivable: (i) household wealth — Chinese urban parents hold property and savings that can fund a non-working adult child, whereas Indonesian households were still drawing down savings (76.3%) merely to cover normal expenses in 2026; and (ii) a dense, cheap, delivery-plus-rental infrastructure that makes a room-bound life logistically possible at low cost across many cities. Low-Medium for full withdrawal because Indonesian informal-sector absorption gives young people an always-available fallback (ojol, warung, freelance, family enterprise) — the Indonesian equivalent of lying flat is not lying in bed, it is under-employment that looks like work. Additional accelerant: Indonesia's own political channel means grievance can convert into mobilisation rather than resignation, which paradoxically slows the withdrawal culture while raising political risk.
vektor_transmisi: (c) ALGORITHMIC CONTENT DIFFUSION is the dominant vector and it is already operating: the 老鼠人/低能量 format is a highly portable video grammar (POV shot from bed, dark room, delivery bag, reversed clock) that survives translation, and TikTok — the same ByteDance recommendation stack that carried it in China — reaches ~180 million Indonesians. Indonesian-language explainers of 'manusia tikus' appeared in 2025 and the raw local equivalents (mager, rebahan, nolep) provide instant subtitling. (b) LOCAL COPYCAT/RELABELLING is the second vector: Indonesian creators will not import the Chinese word; they will mint a local one — expect a bahasa-gaul successor to 'kaum rebahan' and 'nolep' with an explicit economic-futility framing. (a) DIRECT ENTRY OF CHINESE PLAYERS matters indirectly rather than directly: it is not that Chinese firms export the culture, but that the Chinese-platform consumption stack that makes withdrawal survivable (ultra-cheap food delivery, sub-Rp 15,000 meal bundles, Shopee/TikTok Shop/Temu-style cheap goods, cloud/idle gaming, short-drama apps — several of them Chinese-origin) is being installed in Indonesia now; that infrastructure is the true carrier. (d) CHINESE VENTURE CAPITAL is a weak vector for the culture but a strong one for the infrastructure (short-drama, mini-game, live-stream and cheap-delivery investment). (e) DIASPORA/ALUMNI is a real but narrow channel — the rat-person vlog was itself invented by Chinese students abroad, and Indonesian students in China (and in Australia, UK, Japan, Korea) plus the large Indonesian TikTok-Chinese-content translation ecosystem carry the frame home. A SIXTH vector specific to this topic: ACADEMIC AND MEDIA IMPORT — Indonesian universities, think-tanks and journalists have begun using 'tang ping', 'involution' and 'rat people' as analytical labels for Indonesian conditions, which legitimises the frame faster than organic adoption would.
prasyarat_struktural: THRESHOLDS AND INDONESIA'S POSITION VERSUS CHINA AT ITS TRIGGER POINT. (1) Higher-education mass participation outrunning graduate-job creation. China: gross tertiary enrolment ~60.8% (2024) and 12.2-12.7 million graduates a year when lying flat matured. Indonesia: gross tertiary enrolment ~45% (2023), projected to add ~4.3 million students over the next decade toward ~13 million enrolled. Indonesia is BELOW the Chinese threshold but rising, and is projected to become the world's third-largest university system by 2035 — meaning the graduate-oversupply pressure will intensify structurally through the 2030s. (2) Income level at onset. China's lying-flat moment came at roughly USD 12,000-13,000 GDP per capita; Indonesia is around USD 5,000. This is the single biggest divergence: Indonesia is hitting Chinese-level youth unemployment at roughly one-third the income, which makes withdrawal materially unaffordable but makes the emotional content MORE resonant, not less. (3) Urbanisation and rental-room living. China's rat-people archetype presupposes a single young adult living alone in a rented urban room. China is ~67% urban; Indonesia ~58-59% and, crucially, Indonesian urban youth far more often live in the family home or a kos with dense social surveillance — which suppresses invisible withdrawal. (4) Cheap delivery and low-cost consumption stack. A room-bound life requires sub-USD 2 meal delivery at national scale. Indonesia has this in Jabodetabek and major cities via GoFood/GrabFood/ShopeeFood promotions, but at higher real cost relative to income than China. (5) Digital saturation. Indonesia already exceeds the threshold: 80.5% internet penetration, ~22 hours/week of social video. (6) Family safety net without state safety net. China's version is financed by parental property wealth; Indonesia has neither the parental wealth nor unemployment insurance of meaningful duration (JKP coverage is narrow and formal-sector only) — so the Indonesian variant must be work-adjacent. (7) A salient credential-devaluation signal. Indonesia already has it: tertiary TPT (6.13%) above national TPT (4.68%), and 1.03 million unemployed degree-holders.
indikator_pemantauan: Leading indicators that the trend is arriving in force: (1) BPS Sakernas — sustained rise in the 15-24 TPT above 17% AND, more diagnostically, a FALL in the youth labour-force participation rate alongside it (withdrawal shows up as LFPR decline, not unemployment); track also the 'never worked' share of young unemployed (2.81 million of 3.93 million in Aug 2024). (2) The NEET series — movement of the ~9.9 million Gen Z NEET figure toward 11-12 million, and a rising MALE share (currently female-dominated for care reasons; a male shift signals genuine discouragement, not domestic work). (3) Google Trends / TikTok hashtag volumes in Indonesian for a native withdrawal label (successors to 'mager', 'nolep', 'kaum rebahan'; watch for a coined term such as 'manusia tikus', 'generasi gelap' or a fresh slang noun) and for 'burnout', 'resign', 'kerja gak worth it', '#KaburAjaDulu'. (4) Emigration proxies: BP2MI/KP2MI placement data, working-holiday and Japan/Korea/Germany visa applications, IELTS test volumes, passport issuance among under-30s. (5) Employer-side indicators: JobStreet/Kalibrr posting-to-application ratios for fresh graduates, starting-salary stagnation in real terms, and the share of graduate hires in non-graduate roles. (6) Consumption tells: growth in single-serving cheap meal bundles, kos/co-living occupancy at the low end, night-time delivery order share (22:00-04:00), mobile-game and short-drama night-time DAU, sleep-aid and instant-noodle volumes. (7) Institutional tells: universities creating career-anxiety/mental-health units; Kemnaker or Kemendiktisaintek publishing a youth-specific employment package; the appearance of an Indonesian 'anti-involution' or 'anti-hustle' policy vocabulary. (8) Mental-health system load: national helpline volumes, campus counselling waiting lists, and any repeat of I-NAMHS showing deterioration from the 34.9% baseline.
hambatan_transfer: (1) ECONOMIC: Indonesian young people mostly cannot afford non-participation. Household savings are already being drawn down (76.3% dipping into savings), the middle class shrank to 46.7 million in 2025, and there is no unemployment benefit of meaningful scope — so the cost of a month in bed is borne directly by a family that cannot absorb it. (2) SOCIAL-STRUCTURAL: extended-family and neighbourhood density (kos culture, RT/RW, mosque and church networks, kampung sociality) makes invisible withdrawal socially expensive in a way that atomised Chinese one-child urban households do not. (3) RELIGIOUS-NORMATIVE: work-as-ibadah framing and strong intergenerational obligation norms give idleness a moral charge that Chinese secular-Confucian achievement culture frames differently (China's youth rebelled against a productivity ethic; Indonesia's youth face a religious-familial obligation ethic that is harder to satirise publicly). (4) LABOUR-MARKET SHAPE: an ~59-60% informal sector plus a huge gig layer means there is almost always SOMETHING to do for cash, which converts would-be lying-flat into underemployment. (5) DEMOGRAPHIC-STRUCTURAL: Indonesia's tertiary participation (~45%) is still well below China's (60.8%), so the specific pathology of surplus graduates is at maybe two-thirds of Chinese intensity today. (6) POLITICAL-CHANNEL SUBSTITUTION: an open (if contested) protest space means grievance has a public outlet; passive withdrawal competes with active mobilisation for the same energy. (7) LANGUAGE/PLATFORM: Chinese-origin memes still require translation and re-anchoring; the specific rat imagery (sewer rat, 鼠鼠) carries connotations that do not map cleanly onto Indonesian symbolic registers.
faktor_pembatal_transfer: Conditions that mean the Chinese form will NOT be replicated one-to-one in Indonesia, however severe youth unemployment becomes. (1) NO PARENTAL WEALTH BUFFER. The Chinese variant is quietly financed by a generation of urban parents who own appreciated property, hold high savings rates, and — because of the one-child policy — concentrate all resources on a single child; this is what makes 全职儿女 ('full-time children' on a parental allowance) possible. Indonesian families have low home equity in liquid terms, ~2.3-2.5 children per household historically, and are themselves net dissavers right now. A paid 'full-time child' is not a viable Indonesian social role at scale. (2) NO STATE INCOME FLOOR FOR THE YOUNG. China at least offers dense subsidised training, hiring subsidies and rural fallback (village land rights, hukou-linked homestead); Indonesian youth have neither land-right fallback of similar strength nor a youth benefit — Kartu Prakerja is a training stipend, not income support. (3) DIFFERENT LABOUR-MARKET GEOMETRY. China's distress is a graduate-glut problem inside a formalised urban economy; Indonesia's is a formal-job-scarcity problem inside an informal economy with premature deindustrialisation. Indonesia's youth are more likely to be invisibly under-employed than visibly unemployed, so the culture that emerges will valorise 'working hard for nothing' (a hustle-fatigue culture) rather than 'refusing to work' (a withdrawal culture). (4) ARCHIPELAGIC GEOGRAPHY AND LOGISTICS COST. The room-bound life is subsidised in China by a delivery network of extreme density and cost efficiency. Outside Jabodetabek, Surabaya, Bandung, Medan and Makassar, Indonesian delivery economics cannot support a Rp 10,000-15,000 hot meal at scale — the rat-person life is not logistically available in most of the country. (5) HOUSING PATTERN. Solo occupancy in a private flat is a Chinese urban norm and an Indonesian exception; Indonesian young adults live with family or in shared kos far longer, and cohabitation destroys the privacy withdrawal requires. (6) YOUNGER DEMOGRAPHIC POSITION. China's youth despair is amplified by a shrinking cohort facing an ageing dependency burden; Indonesia is still inside a demographic bonus window to roughly 2035-2045, which changes the emotional register from terminal decline to squandered opportunity — anger rather than resignation. (7) OPEN EXIT OPTION. Indonesians can, and increasingly do, emigrate (#KaburAjaDulu); Chinese youth face harder exit friction, which pushes their coping inward.
tahun_masuk_indonesia: Already entered — 2024-2025. The discursive entry point is December 2024 to February 2025 (#KaburAjaDulu going viral) plus the 2025 Indonesian-language coverage of China's 'manusia tikus'. The structural entry point is 2024-2026: youth TPT at 16.26-16.36%, ~9.9 million NEET Gen Z, and unemployed degree-holders crossing 1 million and still rising in February 2026. Treat 2025 as the year the frame became legible in Indonesia and 2026 as the year the data made it undeniable.
tahun_mainstream_indonesia: 2027-2029 [uncertain]. Mainstreaming requires three things to co-occur: (i) a native Indonesian label for withdrawal that trends nationally rather than an imported one; (ii) youth TPT sustained above ~17% together with a visible decline in youth labour-force participation; and (iii) mass-market commercial adoption of the aesthetic (brands and advertisers speaking in the voice of the exhausted non-striver, as Meituan and Tmall did in China within a month of the meme breaking). The Chinese sequence from named condition to brand co-optation ran about four years (2021 tang ping -> 2025 rat-people commercialisation); Indonesia should run it faster because the media stack is denser and the reference case already exists — hence 2-4 years from the 2025 entry point.
tahun_puncak_indonesia: 2030-2034 [uncertain], with a plausible earlier local peak in 2027-2028 if a recession hits. The reasoning: Indonesia's graduate cohort keeps expanding through the 2030s (projected ~13 million enrolled by 2035, third largest system in the world), so the arithmetic mismatch between credentials and graduate-grade jobs worsens for at least another decade; the demographic-bonus window closing around 2035-2045 is the natural point where 'squandered opportunity' becomes 'permanent decline' emotionally. A single-year shock (rupiah crisis, commodity bust, a large formal-sector layoff wave, or AI displacement of entry-level white-collar work) could pull the peak forward to 2027-2029.
skenario_percepatan: Fastest accelerants, roughly in order of impact: (1) AI displacement of entry-level white-collar work (admin, customer service, junior analytics, content) removing the very rungs graduates use to enter; (2) a macro shock — rupiah/commodity crisis or a large-scale manufacturing/textile layoff wave — that pushes national TPT above 6%; (3) a viral Indonesian-language withdrawal label plus a hit short-drama or creator archetype that makes it aspirational-ironic; (4) continued real-wage stagnation with rising costs (VAT/tax changes, subsidised-fuel adjustments, housing costs) so that working full-time visibly fails to deliver a livable outcome; (5) closure of the emigration valve (visa tightening in Japan/Korea/Australia/Germany) which would redirect #KaburAjaDulu energy from exit back into withdrawal; (6) repression of the protest channel, which converts VOICE into passive refusal — the single most likely mechanism by which Indonesia would move from the 2025 protest mode toward the Chinese withdrawal mode; (7) cheap, dense delivery and micro-living infrastructure reaching tier-2 cities, making the room-bound life logistically affordable outside Jabodetabek.
dampak_lapangan_kerja: JOBS LOST OR ERODED: (a) entry-level white-collar roles are already the scarcest resource — the pipeline problem is not that jobs vanish but that graduate-grade first jobs never appear, leaving 1.03 million unemployed degree-holders (Feb 2026); (b) hustle-dependent business models lose their labour subsidy — startups, agencies, retail and F&B that ran on unpaid overtime, 'kerja rodi' culture and passion-washing will face refusal, higher turnover and quiet quitting (63% of under-30 workers reporting deliberate disengagement [uncertain]); (c) MLM, 'financial freedom' coaching, hustle-influencer and side-hustle-course economies lose credibility as the anti-hustle frame spreads; (d) roles requiring long unsocial hours with low pay (retail floor, call centre, field sales) face chronic vacancy. JOBS CHANGED: recruitment and HR shift from screening for 'willingness to sacrifice' to designing for retention, boundaries, hybrid work and mental-health support; management practice must shift from presence-based to output-based supervision; the ojol/gig layer becomes the de facto absorber and shock-buffer of graduate under-employment, exactly as delivery did in China. JOBS CREATED: youth mental-health services (counsellors, campus psychologists, teletherapy — Riliv/Halodoc-type platforms), career-transition and skills-bootcamp providers, employer-side employee-wellbeing and HR-compliance roles, the 'stay-at-home economy' supply chain (night-time delivery, micro-living/co-living operators, short-drama and idle-game production, sleep and comfort products), plus the creator economy itself where the withdrawal aesthetic becomes monetisable content. NET: this trend does not primarily destroy jobs — it destroys the WILLINGNESS to supply cheap labour to bad jobs, and it converts hidden unemployment into visible disengagement, which is a productivity problem before it is an employment problem.
dampak_kelas_menengah: This trend is a middle-class disease specifically — it attacks the class whose entire strategy is credential-based mobility. Indonesia's middle class shrank to ~46.7 million in 2025 (-1.1 million y/y, worse than 2024's -400,000) with ~142 million 'aspiring middle class' below it; the household bargain — sell land or take debt to fund a degree, expect a formal salaried job in return — is visibly failing when tertiary TPT (6.13%) exceeds national TPT (4.68%). Consequences: (1) INTERGENERATIONAL CONFLICT — parents who paid for the degree read withdrawal as ingratitude, producing exactly the family friction Chinese 'full-time children' households report; (2) DELAYED FAMILY FORMATION — Indonesian marriage registrations and fertility are already trending down, and China's experience shows youth economic despair translating into a decade of falling marriages and a birth collapse; Indonesia risks compressing its demographic-bonus window from the demand side; (3) CONSUMPTION DOWNGRADE AND DOOM SPENDING SIMULTANEOUSLY — the same cohort trades down on staples (frugal living, makan tabungan at 76.3%) while spending disproportionately on small emotional purchases (coffee, gacha/blind box, mobile games, short-form entertainment), which is precisely the Chinese 'emotional consumption' pattern; (4) SAVINGS AND ASSET FORMATION COLLAPSE — a cohort that never accumulates housing equity in its twenties will be structurally poorer at fifty, converting a cyclical problem into a permanent class demotion; (5) POLITICAL VOLATILITY — the August 2025 protests were disproportionately a middle-class-adjacent youth phenomenon, and thwarted middle-class expectation is historically the most politically combustible condition in Indonesia.
dampak_daerah_non_jawa: Not a Java-only phenomenon, but it takes two different forms. IN BIG CITIES (Jabodetabek, Bandung, Surabaya, Semarang, Yogyakarta, plus Medan, Makassar, Denpasar, Balikpapan, Pekanbaru): the full Chinese-style pattern is possible — rented kos, delivery-fed, nocturnal, socially isolated — because the delivery, co-living and mobile-entertainment infrastructure exists. Yogyakarta and Malang are particularly exposed: student cities with huge graduate outputs, low local wage ceilings and cheap kos, i.e. the exact conditions for post-graduation stasis. OUTSIDE THOSE CITIES: the withdrawal form is materially unavailable (no cheap delivery density, no solo housing, high family surveillance), so the same economic distress expresses as (a) return migration to the family home and absorption into farm, fishery or family-trade work that looks like employment but is disguised underemployment; (b) out-migration to Java or abroad (PMI placement); (c) NEET status among young women in particular, which is already the dominant Indonesian NEET pattern. There is also an important regional asymmetry in the DATA: provinces with high youth unemployment (Aceh, West Java, Banten, Maluku, North Sulawesi have historically ranked high) will show the labour symptom first, while the CULTURAL symptom will appear first in Java's student cities and be exported outward by returning graduates and by TikTok. Policy implication: an anti-withdrawal strategy targeted only at Jakarta will miss the larger, quieter non-Java version, where the failure mode is invisible underemployment and female NEET status rather than viral nocturnal vlogs.
jurusan_terancam: Programmes whose value proposition is 'generic white-collar credential' are the most exposed, because they are exactly what China cut. Chinese precedent is explicit: information management and information systems, and public affairs management, were the two most frequently revoked undergraduate programmes (100 and 97 universities respectively, 2018-2022), and management and arts programmes dominated the cuts, with low employment rates the stated criterion. Indonesian analogues at risk: (1) Manajemen and Administrasi Bisnis/Administrasi Publik/Administrasi Niaga in the vast non-selective private-university tier — enormous enrolment, weak differentiation, entry roles most exposed to AI automation; (2) Akuntansi at the transactional end (bookkeeping, AP/AR) as automation and shared-service centres absorb the work; (3) Ilmu Komunikasi in its generic form — massively over-enrolled relative to the shrinking number of paid media/PR entry roles; (4) Sekretari, Perkantoran and general D3 office administration; (5) Pendidikan (teacher-training) beyond the number of actual teacher vacancies, which is why Indonesia's 2026 programme-closure round explicitly avoided touching education programmes — a political constraint China did not face in the same way; (6) low-selectivity Hukum, Sosiologi, Ilmu Politik and Sastra where the programme does not connect to a licensed profession; (7) generic Sistem Informasi/Informatika at institutions without real project or lab capacity — the credential exists but the capability does not, which is the fastest route to a devalued degree. The deeper threat is not the discipline but the TIER: Indonesia has thousands of small private institutions whose graduates carry the credential cost without the credential's labour-market power, which is the structural engine of Kong-Yiji-style despair.
jurusan_dibutuhkan: Follow China's replacement pattern, adapted to Indonesia's industrial base. China cut 12,200 programmes over 2021-2025 while opening ~10,200, plus 2,600+ 'micro-majors' and 1,100+ professional training courses, concentrated in AI, integrated circuits, robotics, biomanufacturing, low-altitude economy, new energy, elderly care and digital health. Indonesia's high-demand set: (1) AI/machine learning and data engineering — already appearing (UI's S1 Kecerdasan Artifisial from 2026/2027, Unesa's S1 AI, D4 Teknologi Informasi dan Kecerdasan Artifisial) but at tiny quotas relative to need; (2) applied engineering tied to real industry — mechatronics, industrial automation, electrical/energy systems, mining and mineral processing (hilirisasi nickel/copper/bauxite), petrochemicals; (3) healthcare and care work — nursing, physiotherapy, geriatric and mental-health care, plus care-work qualifications recognised in Japan/Germany/Korea, which doubles as an emigration pathway; (4) mental-health professionals — Indonesia's psychologist-to-population ratio is grossly inadequate against a 34.9% adolescent mental-health problem rate; this trend itself creates the demand; (5) agri-food technology, aquaculture and food processing — the sectors that can absorb non-Java graduates where they live; (6) skilled trades with formal certification (welding, HVAC, electrical, marine, aviation MRO) — the Indonesian answer to China's vocational-undergraduate push; (7) cross-cutting employability skills as credentialed micro-programmes: applied English/Mandarin/Japanese, AI-tool fluency, project delivery, sales — the 'micro-major' instrument China deployed at scale. Crucially, the demanded skill for THIS trend specifically is the ability to work in low-supervision, output-based, hybrid environments — self-management, not endurance.
china_education_response: China's education system responded with unusual bluntness and speed, and it is the most transferable part of the Chinese playbook. (1) SUPPLY-SIDE PURGE: a March 2023 guideline from the Ministry of Education plus four other departments required roughly 20% of higher-education discipline and programme offerings to be optimised or adjusted; between 2021 and 2025 universities ended or suspended 12,200 undergraduate programmes and introduced about 10,200 new ones, affecting more than 30% of all undergraduate programmes nationally. Low employment rates and misalignment with industrial upgrading were the explicit criteria; management and arts bore the brunt (information management and information systems, and public affairs management, were the most-revoked programmes). (2) REDIRECTION TOWARD AI AND STRATEGIC INDUSTRY: new and renamed programmes cluster in artificial intelligence, integrated circuits, robotics, new energy, biomanufacturing and elderly care; even elite 985 institutions cut legacy majors while adding thousands of new ones. (3) MODULARISATION: 2,600+ 'micro-majors' (微专业) and 1,100+ professional training courses were created to retrofit employability onto existing degrees without waiting for full curriculum reform — a fast, cheap instrument Indonesia could copy immediately. (4) VOCATIONAL ELEVATION: expansion of vocational undergraduate (职业本科) capacity and a revised Vocational Education Law to reduce the stigma that pushes everyone into academic degrees. (5) EMPLOYMENT-LINKED ACCOUNTABILITY: graduate employment outcomes became a formal input into programme approval and continuation — with the well-documented side effect of statistical gaming (see unintended_consequences). (6) MASS RETRAINING: a target to train 1 million graduates and youths in 2025 for employability, alongside subsidised internships/apprenticeship placements (就业见习). Indonesia's 2026 closure of 122 study programmes and 1,200+ new programme openings is the same instinct at roughly 1% of the Chinese scale and three years later.
respons_kebijakan_china: Sequence and content, with the pre-emptive lesson for Indonesia at each step. (1) 2021 — MORAL CONDEMNATION AND CENSORSHIP: Xinhua called lying flat 'shameful', tang-ping forums and groups were restricted. This FAILED: the term survived, mutated into 摆烂 and 鼠鼠文学, and the state lost the framing initiative. LESSON: do not attempt to shame or suppress the discourse; it converts a coping meme into a political symbol. (2) 2021 — LABOUR-STANDARD ENFORCEMENT: the Supreme People's Court and MOHRSS jointly declared 996 (9am-9pm, six days) illegal in August 2021 via published typical cases, giving the anti-overwork sentiment a legal channel. LESSON: this is the single most adoptable pre-emptive policy — enforce existing working-hour and overtime law loudly and publicly BEFORE the anti-hustle sentiment turns anti-system. (3) 2023 — EDUCATION SUPPLY-SIDE ADJUSTMENT (see china_education_response): cut what does not employ, fund what does, modularise the rest. (4) 2023 — DATA GOVERNANCE, HANDLED BADLY: suspending the youth-unemployment series for six months after it hit 21.3% destroyed credibility and became an international story larger than the number itself; resumption on a student-excluding methodology invited permanent suspicion. LESSON FOR INDONESIA: never suspend or redefine an embarrassing labour series; publish it and pair it with a policy response. (5) 2025 — DEMAND-SIDE HIRING INCENTIVES: 17 inter-ministerial measures (April 2025) from MOHRSS, MOE and MOF — one-off job-expansion subsidies for employers hiring 2025 graduates, graduates unemployed within two years, and registered unemployed youth aged 16-24; social-insurance subsidies; tax and fee reductions; extension of SOE graduate-hiring subsidies to 31 December 2026; a further package in March 2026. (6) 2025 — REFRAMING THE PROBLEM AS SYSTEMIC, NOT INDIVIDUAL: the '反内卷' (anti-involution) campaign launched from Xi's 1 July 2025 Central Financial and Economic Affairs Commission remarks and enshrined in the October 2025 Fourth Plenum decision, targeting destructive competition among firms and local governments. LESSON: naming the structure rather than blaming the young is what finally de-escalated the discourse — Beijing effectively conceded the youth's diagnosis and moved the target. (7) THROUGHOUT — CHANNELLING: rural revitalisation placements, grassroots service schemes, SOE hiring quotas and expanded postgraduate places to warehouse cohorts. LESSON: warehousing buys time but inflates the next cohort's credential arms race, as China's exam-application data now shows.
rekomendasi_kebijakan_indonesia: (1) MEASURE HONESTLY AND MONTHLY. Publish youth (15-24) unemployment, youth LFPR, NEET counts by sex and province, and graduate-underemployment (graduates in non-graduate jobs) as a standing quarterly release. The decisive early-warning variable is youth LFPR FALLING while unemployment rises — that is withdrawal, and Indonesia currently has no timely indicator for it. Do not repeat China's 2023 suspension error. (2) ENFORCE WORKING-HOUR LAW NOW, PUBLICLY. Kemnaker should run a visible campaign of overtime and working-hour enforcement (UU Ketenagakerjaan/Cipta Kerja provisions) plus a right-to-disconnect norm for white-collar employers, before anti-hustle sentiment hardens into anti-work sentiment. This is the highest-yield pre-emptive move and it is nearly free. (3) TARGETED DEMAND-SIDE HIRING SUBSIDY. Copy the Chinese instrument precisely: a time-limited BPJS-contribution subsidy plus a wage subsidy for employers hiring first-time workers aged 18-24, with a heavier rate for non-Java placements and for SMEs — cheaper and faster-acting than another training scheme. (4) FIX PRAKERJA'S THEORY OF CHANGE. Shift from generic online course vouchers to employer-committed apprenticeships (magang bersertifikat with a hiring commitment), modelled on China's 就业见习; pay employers for conversion to permanent hire, not for training delivery. (5) HIGHER-EDUCATION SUPPLY DISCIPLINE WITH TRANSPARENCY. Kemendiktisaintek should publish programme-level graduate employment and earnings outcomes (a tracer-study mandate with audited data) and tie new-programme approval and accreditation to them — but avoid China's error of making employment rate a pure survival metric, which produced systematic falsification. Pair closure with funded transition for affected students and staff. (6) MICRO-CREDENTIALS AT SCALE. Deploy an Indonesian equivalent of China's 2,600 micro-majors — 1-2 semester stackable certificates in AI tooling, data, industrial automation, care work, applied languages — retrofittable onto existing degrees within one year. (7) BUILD YOUTH MENTAL-HEALTH CAPACITY BEFORE THE PEAK. Against a 34.9% adolescent mental-health-problem baseline and a severe psychologist shortage, fund campus counselling, a national youth helpline, and BPJS Kesehatan coverage for outpatient mental health — the cheapest intervention with the highest social return if withdrawal culture arrives. (8) KEEP THE VOICE CHANNEL OPEN. The August 2025 protests and the repression response are directly relevant: closing the political outlet is the surest way to convert Indonesian youth anger into Chinese-style withdrawal. Institutionalised youth consultation (a standing national youth employment council with real agenda power) is cheaper than the alternative. (9) TREAT EMIGRATION AS POLICY, NOT LEAKAGE. #KaburAjaDulu is a pressure valve; formalise it — bilateral labour agreements with Japan, Korea, Germany, Australia and the Gulf for skilled and care roles, with certification, protection and remittance/return incentives, instead of moralising about disloyalty (the same mistake Xinhua made about lying flat).
peluang_bisnis: (1) AFFORDABLE MENTAL HEALTH AT SCALE — teletherapy, group therapy, campus-embedded counselling, corporate EAP for mid-size Indonesian employers, and AI-assisted triage; a 34.9% adolescent problem rate against a tiny professional supply is the widest service gap this trend creates. (2) THE STAY-AT-HOME ('rebahan') ECONOMY — night-window delivery (22:00-04:00 order share is a leading indicator and an underserved slot), single-serving cheap meal bundles, ready-to-eat and frozen at sub-Rp 20,000 price points, comfort/sleep goods, micro-living and co-living operators offering dignified small-format urban rooms. (3) LOW-COMMITMENT ENTERTAINMENT — short dramas (the fastest-growing Chinese format and already entering Indonesia), idle and hyper-casual mobile games, audio and podcast, cloud gaming: the products of an economy where time is abundant and money is not. (4) 'DIGNIFIED EXIT' SERVICES — emigration and study-abroad services, IELTS/JLPT/TOPIK prep, care-worker and welder certification for Japan/Germany/Korea placement, and remittance/fintech products for a young overseas cohort; #KaburAjaDulu is a market, not just a hashtag. (5) EMPLOYABILITY INFRASTRUCTURE — bootcamps with hiring guarantees, apprenticeship-brokerage platforms, skills-verification and portfolio credentials, and AI-tool fluency training; also HR-tech for output-based management, which employers will need as presence-based supervision collapses. (6) SECOND-HAND, REPAIR AND RENTAL — the consumption pattern of a cohort with time but no income (already visible in the thrift/preloved boom); the Chinese analogue (Xianyu) is a multi-hundred-million-user platform. (7) CREATOR ECONOMY AROUND THE AESTHETIC ITSELF — Indonesian brands that speak in the exhausted-non-striver voice will out-perform hustle-coded advertising with under-30s; the Chinese precedent (Meituan, Tmall, 1688, Midea joining the rat-people meme within weeks in March-April 2025) shows this is a first-mover advantage measured in weeks. (8) FINANCIAL PRODUCTS FOR IRREGULAR INCOME — micro-savings, income-smoothing and insurance designed for gig/irregular earners rather than salaried workers. CAUTION: several of these monetise distress; the reputational line between serving and exploiting a demoralised cohort is thin, and predatory paylater/gambling products are already occupying the same emotional space.
rekomendasi_individu_mahasiswa: (1) BUILD A VERIFIABLE PORTFOLIO, NOT JUST A TRANSCRIPT — in a credential-devalued market (tertiary TPT 6.13% above national 4.68%), demonstrable output beats the degree; ship real projects, internships, freelance work, open-source or community work with evidence. (2) BECOME AI-COMPLEMENTARY, FAST — the roles most at risk are the entry-level white-collar rungs; the defensible position is being the person who directs AI tools within a domain (finance, health, logistics, agriculture, law), not the person who does the task AI now does. (3) ACQUIRE ONE PHYSICALLY OR REGULATORILY ANCHORED SKILL — care work, industrial maintenance, electrical, welding, aquaculture, medical technology, or a licensed profession; these resist both automation and offshoring, and they are the skills with formal overseas demand. (4) LANGUAGE AS AN OPTION ON EXIT — English to professional level plus one of Japanese/Korean/German/Mandarin converts the emigration option from fantasy into a plan; this is rational hedging, not disloyalty. (5) TREAT YOUR FIRST JOB AS A LEARNING PURCHASE, NOT AN IDENTITY — but refuse unpaid overtime as a norm; the anti-hustle instinct is correct in substance and needs to be expressed as boundary-setting and output discipline rather than disengagement, because quiet quitting damages the quitter's skill accumulation most. (6) PROTECT SLEEP, DAYLIGHT AND ONE OFFLINE SOCIAL ANCHOR — the rat-person trajectory begins with reversed sleep and ends with unemployability; circadian collapse and social withdrawal are the two mechanisms that turn a bad year into a lost decade. Concretely: fixed wake time, morning daylight, one weekly in-person commitment. (7) BUILD A SMALL INCOME FLOOR EARLY — 3-6 months of expenses, however modest, is what converts 'I must accept this exploitative job' into 'I can choose'; without it, anti-hustle sentiment has no material backing. (8) FIND OR FORM A COHORT — the single strongest protective factor against withdrawal is a peer group with shared structure (study group, co-working, community organisation, religious or sports community). (9) READ THE MACRO — track BPS releases on youth employment and sectoral hiring; choosing a sector with structural tailwinds (energy transition, healthcare, food, defence-adjacent industry, downstream minerals) beats optimising a CV inside a shrinking one.
rekomendasi_perguruan_tinggi: (1) PUBLISH PROGRAMME-LEVEL OUTCOMES AND ACT ON THEM — mandatory audited tracer studies with employment and earnings by programme, published; then close, merge or radically redesign the bottom decile, following China's 2021-2025 purge logic but with student-transition funding attached. (2) SHRINK GENERIC MANAGEMENT/ADMINISTRATION/COMMUNICATION INTAKE and reallocate the seats to applied engineering, health and care, agri-food technology and AI/data — mirroring the specific programmes China revoked (information management and information systems; public affairs management). (3) INTRODUCE MICRO-CREDENTIALS WITHIN 12 MONTHS — a stackable 1-2 semester certificate layer (AI tooling, data analysis, industrial automation, care work, applied Japanese/German/Mandarin, sales and project delivery) retrofitted onto existing degrees; this is China's 2,600-micro-major instrument and it is the fastest, cheapest lever an Indonesian university actually controls. (4) MAKE INDUSTRY PLACEMENT A GRADUATION REQUIREMENT, NOT A BONUS — a minimum one-semester supervised placement with a named employer partner for every applied programme; convert the MBKM legacy into enforceable employer commitments rather than administrative reporting. (5) BUILD REAL CAREER AND MENTAL-HEALTH SERVICES — a funded ratio of counsellors and career advisers per 1,000 students, with proactive outreach to students who stop attending (attendance drop-off is the earliest detectable signal of withdrawal); Indonesian campuses currently detect this far too late. (6) ELEVATE VOCATIONAL PATHWAYS AND DESTIGMATISE THEM — expand applied/vocational bachelor capacity (Indonesia's 2026 programme growth is already vocational-weighted) and give it parity in funding, faculty quality and employer recognition, as China did with 职业本科. (7) TEACH THE ECONOMICS OF THEIR OWN SITUATION — a required module on labour-market reality, AI displacement, financial resilience and boundary-setting at work; students who understand the structural cause are measurably less likely to internalise failure as personal defect, which is the psychological mechanism the Chinese rat-people culture runs on. (8) STOP SELLING DEGREES THE MARKET DOES NOT WANT — the ethical core: small private institutions charging tuition for programmes with known-poor outcomes are manufacturing the Indonesian Kong Yiji cohort, and accreditation policy should make that unprofitable.
dampak_negatif_china: (1) DEMOGRAPHIC DAMAGE, the most consequential and now irreversible in the medium term: marriage registrations have fallen for a decade and are roughly half their peak; births fell to about 7.92 million in 2025 from 9.54 million in the 2024 dragon-year rebound [uncertain on the exact 2025 figure] — young people cite cost, job insecurity and long hours as reasons. Lying flat began as a lifestyle meme and ended as a fertility outcome. (2) LABOUR SUPPLY AND HUMAN-CAPITAL WASTE: multi-year gaps between graduation and first employment produce permanent skill scarring; graduates absorbed into delivery and livestream work inside a ~200-million flexible-employment pool represent a large stock of unused tertiary investment. (3) DEFENSIVE CREDENTIAL ARMS RACE: 3.718 million people cleared screening for ~38,100 civil-service posts in the 2026 exam (a record, ~2.9x 2019), with individual posts above 7,000:1 — millions of person-years spent on zero-sum exam preparation rather than production. (4) MENTAL HEALTH: depressive disorders among ages 5-24 are rising, and the withdrawal lifestyle (reversed sleep, no daylight, no social contact) is itself a risk multiplier for depression regardless of its origin. (5) DEMAND DEFICIENCY AND DEFLATION: a generation that refuses to consume is one of the transmission channels of China's weak domestic demand — 'low desire' is a macroeconomic condition, not just an attitude, and the anti-involution campaign is partly an attempt to fix the resulting price-war spiral. (6) INSTITUTIONAL CREDIBILITY DAMAGE: the six-month suspension of the youth-unemployment series in 2023 and the well-documented gaming of graduate employment statistics eroded trust in official data — a lasting cost that made every subsequent good number less believable. (7) INTERGENERATIONAL STRAIN: the 'full-time children' arrangement transfers the cost of youth unemployment onto retiring parents' savings, weakening household balance sheets exactly when China needs consumption. (8) NORMALISATION OF DEFEAT: the deepest damage is that a cohort has developed a fluent, funny, socially rewarded vocabulary for its own defeat, which lowers the psychological cost of not trying — the hardest thing for any policy to reverse.
risiko_sosial_indonesia: (1) LOST GENERATION AT A LOWER INCOME LEVEL: Indonesia is reaching Chinese-level youth unemployment (16.36%) at roughly one-third of China's income per capita and without unemployment insurance, family property wealth or a state training system of Chinese density — the same distress with a far thinner cushion, meaning worse and faster human damage. (2) WASTE OF THE DEMOGRAPHIC BONUS: with Gen Z at ~74.93 million (27.94% of the population) and the bonus window closing around 2035-2045, a decade of youth disengagement would mean the bonus expires unconverted — Indonesia would become old before it becomes rich, which is precisely the trap China is now in. (3) POLITICAL VOLATILITY, NOT QUIET WITHDRAWAL: the more likely Indonesian failure mode is not bedrooms but streets — August 2025 (30+ provinces, ~3,195 detained, a death that catalysed nationwide anger) is the template; economically hopeless, digitally coordinated youth are the most combustible political input Indonesia has, and repression would accelerate rather than resolve it. (4) MENTAL-HEALTH SYSTEM OVERWHELM: a 34.9% adolescent mental-health-problem baseline meeting mass graduate unemployment, against a psychologist shortage, points to rising self-harm and suicide risk with almost no service capacity to absorb it. (5) PREDATORY ECONOMY CAPTURE: demoralised, time-rich, cash-poor young people are the target market for online gambling (already a national crisis), illegal paylater and pinjol, crypto/trading gambling, MLM and 'quick money' scams, and — most seriously — trafficking into Southeast Asian scam compounds, which already recruits heavily from unemployed Indonesian graduates via fake overseas job offers. This is the single most dangerous Indonesian-specific pathway, and it has no Chinese equivalent in the same form. (6) RADICALISATION AND EXTREMIST RECRUITMENT: idle, alienated, online-native young men are a historically documented recruitment pool for both religious extremism and organised crime in Indonesia. (7) GENDERED WITHDRAWAL BECOMING PERMANENT: Indonesia's ~9.9 million NEET Gen Z are already female-dominated; an anti-hustle norm risks re-domesticating young women permanently under a voluntary-sounding label, entrenching a labour-force participation gap. (8) EMIGRATION OF THE MOST CAPABLE: #KaburAjaDulu selects for the employable — English-speaking, skilled, mobile — so the withdrawal culture stays home while the talent leaves, a doubly adverse selection.
unintended_consequences: IN CHINA: (a) statistical gaming — tying programme survival to graduate employment rates produced widespread falsification of employment records (students pressured to submit fake employment contracts), corrupting the very data the policy depended on; (b) the suspension of the youth-unemployment series made the number MORE famous, not less; (c) suppressing lying-flat discourse simply generated successor vocabulary every 12-24 months (摆烂, 鼠鼠, 孔乙己, 老鼠人) — an unkillable semantic hydra; (d) commercial co-optation defanged the politics but also normalised the identity: when Meituan and Tmall market to 'rat people', being one becomes a consumer segment rather than a crisis; (e) expanding postgraduate places to absorb unemployment inflated the next cohort's credential requirements, making the arms race worse — and the 2026 data (kaoyan applications falling for a third year while civil-service applications hit a record) shows students have now priced in that a master's no longer helps; (f) the anti-involution campaign aimed at firms has begun to be read by youth as vindication, which improves sentiment but raises expectations the economy may not meet. IN INDONESIA (predicted): (a) hustle-culture backlash could be absorbed by employers as an excuse to offer worse jobs ('Gen Z does not want to work anyway') rather than better ones — blaming the worker for a demand-side failure; (b) closing under-performing study programmes without transition funding would strand exactly the low-income students the policy is meant to help; (c) promoting entrepreneurship as the answer to graduate unemployment (the standard Indonesian policy reflex) tends to push young people into under-capitalised micro-businesses with high failure rates, producing a second layer of disillusionment; (d) an anti-hustle norm arriving BEFORE Indonesia has completed industrialisation could suppress the labour intensity a catching-up economy needs — Indonesia may get the anti-work culture of a rich country while still having the income of a middle one; (e) the emigration valve, if it works, will hollow out precisely the skilled cohort needed to fix the domestic problem; (f) the aesthetics of withdrawal are monetisable, so Indonesian creators and brands have a commercial incentive to spread a norm that is socially costly.
kelompok_rentan: (1) FRESH GRADUATES OF LOW-TIER PRIVATE UNIVERSITIES (PTS) — carrying tuition debt or family sacrifice with a credential the market discounts; the core Kong-Yiji cohort, and the most likely first Indonesian rat-people population, concentrated in Java's student cities (Yogyakarta, Malang, Bandung, Semarang, Jabodetabek). (2) SMK GRADUATES — the highest unemployment rate of any education level (7.74%, Feb 2026), trained for manufacturing jobs that premature deindustrialisation is not creating. (3) YOUNG WOMEN — already the majority of Indonesia's ~9.9 million Gen Z NEET; withdrawal that is culturally legible as 'helping at home' is invisible to policy and hardest to reverse. (4) YOUNG MEN AGED 18-25 WITHOUT STABLE WORK — the group most exposed to online gambling, pinjol, scam-compound trafficking, extremist recruitment and street-level political mobilisation. (5) FIRST-GENERATION-TO-UNIVERSITY YOUTH FROM LOWER-MIDDLE-INCOME FAMILIES — the family bet all its savings on the degree; failure carries the heaviest shame load and the least material fallback, and this group sits inside the ~142 million 'aspiring middle class'. (6) YOUTH OUTSIDE JAVA AND IN HIGH-UNEMPLOYMENT PROVINCES — where neither graduate jobs nor the gig fallback exist at scale, so the only options are migration or invisible underemployment. (7) YOUNG PEOPLE WITH EXISTING MENTAL-HEALTH CONDITIONS — against the I-NAMHS baseline (34.9% with a problem, 2.45 million with a disorder) and near-zero service capacity, the withdrawal lifestyle is a clinical accelerant. (8) OJOL AND GIG WORKERS UNDER 30 — the absorbing layer for graduate under-employment, with falling real earnings and no social protection; the death of a 21-year-old ojol driver was the spark for the largest youth unrest in a decade, which is a precise measure of this group's exposure.
kasus_china: CASE 1 — LUO HUAZHONG AND THE ORIGIN TEXT (April-May 2021): a former factory worker posts 'Lying Flat Is Justice' (躺平即是正义) on Baidu Tieba with a photo of himself in bed, describing quitting work, moving somewhere cheap, and living on roughly two months of casual work a year. It becomes the defining text of a generation; Xinhua calls the movement shameful; the post is scrubbed; the word becomes a 2021 buzzword anyway. The lesson is that one authentic post beat the entire propaganda apparatus. CASE 2 — THE 21.3% AND THE BLACKOUT (June-August 2023): youth unemployment hits a record 21.3%, the NBS suspends publication for six months, and resumes on a student-excluding basis; the number becomes an international symbol of Chinese economic distress and the suspension itself becomes the story. CASE 3 — KONG YIJI LITERATURE (March 2023): graduates adopt Lu Xun's failed-scholar character as a self-description — the degree is 'a long gown I cannot take off', i.e. too educated for manual work, not employable for graduate work. It provoked a state-media rebuke telling youth to remove the gown, which backfired. CASE 4 — 老鼠人 GOES COMMERCIAL (March-April 2025): the 'low-energy rat person' vlog format explodes on Douyin and Xiaohongshu, with a single Douyin topic exceeding 1.47 billion views and cross-platform totals reported in the billions; within weeks Meituan, Tmall, Alibaba 1688, Midea, Guoquan and others publish self-deprecating 'we are rat people too' marketing, and Chinese marketing trade press writes about who is 'harvesting the traffic dividend of the low-energy rat people'. A subculture of despair became an advertising segment in under six weeks. CASE 5 — THE EXAM ARMS RACE (2026): 3.718 million applicants pass qualification review for the national civil-service exam (a record, ~2.9x 2019) chasing ~38,100 posts — the first year posts were cut — while postgraduate-exam applications fall for a third straight year to 3.43 million, and civil-service applicants exceed graduate-school applicants for the first time. The market has concluded that only a state job is worth striving for. CASE 6 — THE STATE ADOPTS THE WORD (July-October 2025): '反内卷' — anti-involution — moves from youth slang to Politburo-level economic policy via Xi's 1 July 2025 remarks and the Fourth Plenum decision of October 2025, redirected from individuals to firms and local governments.
padanan_indonesia: (1) #KaburAjaDulu (Dec 2024, viral Feb 2025) — the closest functional equivalent to tang ping: a generational verdict that effort inside the system does not pay. The difference is directional (exit abroad vs. stasis in bed) and it is the key to understanding Indonesia's variant. (2) 'Kaum rebahan', 'mager', 'nolep', 'healing', 'self-reward', 'doom spending' — a fully formed native vocabulary of retreat that predates the Chinese import and gives it a landing pad. (3) QUIET QUITTING AS MASS PRACTICE — 'kerja ya kerja, tapi secukupnya'; Populix (2024) reporting 63%+ of under-30 workers deliberately disengaged and Jakpat (Feb 2026) reporting 41% of Gen Z refusing out-of-hours work [both uncertain]; this is Indonesia's 摆烂 in workplace form. (4) 'SARJANA MENGANGGUR' DISCOURSE — the Indonesian Kong Yiji: 1.03 million unemployed degree-holders (Feb 2026) and a tertiary unemployment rate above the national average, with a growing national argument about whether university is still worth it. (5) THE OJOL ABSORPTION LAYER — graduates driving for Gojek/Grab is the Indonesian analogue of Chinese master's holders in Meituan uniforms, and it is already the dominant coping strategy. (6) THE AUGUST 2025 PROTESTS — Indonesia's structural difference in one image: where Chinese youth went to bed, Indonesian youth went to the street; 30+ provinces, ~3,195 detained, a One Piece pirate flag as the emblem. (7) MEDIA IMPORT OF THE CHINESE FRAME — Indonesian-language coverage of 'manusia tikus' during 2025 by regional and national outlets, which is the observable first step of the meme's transfer.

catatan_kontradiksi_data: (1) THE 17.6% (SEP 2024) FIGURE IN THE BRIEF COULD NOT BE VERIFIED AGAINST A NAMED SOURCE. BPS publishes Sakernas in February and August rounds, not September; the August 2024 round gives ~3.93 million unemployed aged 15-24 and a rate commonly reported as ~16%, while the modelled ILO/World Bank estimate for Indonesia in 2024 is 13.14% and the most recent BPS prints are 16.26% (Nov 2025) and 16.36% (Feb 2026). The brief's 17.6% is plausible for a specific sub-definition (urban only, or a particular quarterly/harmonised series) but should be cited carefully; the safest defensible statement is 'roughly 16-17%, the highest of any age group'. (2) CHINA'S YOUTH-UNEMPLOYMENT SERIES IS NOT COMPARABLE ACROSS THE 2023 BREAK: 21.3% (June 2023) includes job-seeking students; the post-Dec-2023 series excludes them, so the 18.9% record of August 2025 is NOT lower than 2023 in like-for-like terms. Any lag comparison using both numbers must flag this. (3) INDONESIAN HEADLINE UNEMPLOYMENT FOR FEB 2026 APPEARS IN SOURCES AS BOTH 4.68% and 4.91% (the latter is the August 2024 figure being recycled), and the unemployed count as both 7.24 million (Feb 2026) and 7.35 million (Nov 2025) — check the reference period before quoting. (4) 老鼠人 VIEW COUNTS DIVERGE BY AN ORDER OF MAGNITUDE: the research brief cites '>2 billion views'; Chinese marketing sources cite a single Douyin topic at 1.47 billion and aggregate cross-platform figures approaching 20 billion. None are audited platform disclosures. Use '>2 billion' as the conservative floor. (5) CHINA'S 2025 BIRTH FIGURE (7.92 million, down from 9.54 million in 2024) implies an unusually sharp one-year fall; the 2024 number was inflated by the dragon-year effect, but the magnitude should be treated as provisional. (6) INDONESIAN QUIET-QUITTING AND BURNOUT PERCENTAGES (63% disengaged, 41% refusing out-of-hours work, one third burnt out before 25) come from commercial online panels with undisclosed sampling frames and are mutually non-comparable. (7) INDONESIAN TERTIARY GROSS ENROLMENT is quoted as ~45% (World-Bank-style GER, 2023) but as ~31-35% in some Kemendikbud APK PT reporting because of different age-band and institution-coverage definitions — the China comparison (60.8%) should use the same definition on both sides. (8) THE 20-MILLION-JOBLESS-GEN-Z FIGURE for urban China is a media-derived estimate, not an NBS series. (9) INTERPRETIVE CONTRADICTION, not a data one: some analyses read the 2026 fall in Chinese youth unemployment (to 14.9% in June) as genuine improvement, others as the statistical effect of discouraged workers leaving the labour force — which is precisely what a withdrawal culture would produce, and the two readings cannot be distinguished from the published series.
